Performers
Boston Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), Serge Koussevitzky (conductor) Documented[1] [2] [3]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The performing edition and any editorial alterations are not identified in the recording sources.

[1]
Recorded
24 April 1929 Documented

Young lists CVE-48988 with the recording date 24 April 1929, DAHR lists it among the Boston Symphony Orchestra and Koussevitzky recordings of Symphony No. 94 made that day, and the Bolig discography assigns the finale (“Allegro di molto”) to that matrix. Commons’ 1 January 1929 is not a session day.

[4] [3] [6]
Place
Symphony Hall, Boston, Massachusetts, United States Documented

Young heads the 22 April 1929 session “Symphony Hall, Boston, Massachusetts” and lists the 24 April retaken sides of the same symphony under that session; DAHR gives Symphony Hall, Boston for the Andante side CVE-48984. A separate place for the 24 April retakes is not given.

[4] [5]
Label
Victor Documented[2] [5]
Catalogue
Victor set M-55 (discs 7058–⁠7060), released September 1929 Documented

Young lists the symphony as released 9/29 on M-55 (7058/60), with later AM-55, DM-55, HMV and LP issues. The upstream transfer also names set M-55 (Internet Archive description), and DAHR places the Andante on disc 7059. The disc number of this movement’s sides is not stated; the side order (sides 1–⁠2 movement I, sides 3–⁠4 the Andante, sides 5–⁠6 the Menuetto and Finale) suggests 7058 for movement I and 7060 for the Menuetto and Finale, but that allocation is inferred.

[4] [2] [5]
Matrix, take, sides
CVE-48988, take 2 or take 3: the finale; the take on this transfer is not identified Documented

Young lists both take 2 and take 3 of CVE-48988 as issued (three takes made), and Bolig names take 3. Which take the Bob Varney transfer reproduces is not established by any source consulted, so only the matrix is asserted. The DAHR matrix page could not be opened on 17 October 2026 (503 error). No run-out inspection has been made of the digital surrogate.

[4] [6] [3]
Transfer
Bob Varney — transfer from original Victor 78s Documented[2]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is identified. The Internet Archive item was uploaded in December 2008, which is an upload date.

[1] [2]
Processing
Transfer from the original Victor 78 rpm set M-55 into one 20:48 file, from which the four movements were extracted as separate Commons files. Documented

The file lengths of the four Commons movements sum to the length of the Internet Archive file within about a second. The extraction procedure, stylus, playback curve, side-join locations and noise treatment are not documented.

[2] [1]
Composition rights
Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies. Inferred, not documented

Haydn died in 1809. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

[7] [8]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis). Documented

Commons applies PD-EU-audio to the Koussevitzky/Boston recording attributed to 1929, and the Internet Archive item carries a Creative Commons public-domain licence URL, not treated here as authority to waive Victor’s rights. The programme’s pre-1963 European rule applies because the 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension; Young gives the release as September 1929, which supports first publication well before 1963. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US status is not established.

  • PD-EU-audio — European performers’ and producers’ rights claimed expired.
  • Creative Commons public-domain dedication — licence URL on the Internet Archive item.
